subject: Private fleet maintenance: phased network-gated patching and rollback playbook
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: ACME Health <ops@acmehealth.com>, DataCenterCo NOC <dc-ops@datacenterco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private fleet maintenance: proposed dates and gating model

Hi team —

We're preparing a short, non-invasive patch for your private deployment (v1.12.3 -> v1.13.0 small fixes). We want to coordinate a low-risk, network-gated rollout so we can limit blast radius and have a fast rollback. Proposed plan (high level):

- Window: Tue 2028-05-30 01:00–05:00 PDT (customer-preferred), alternate Wed 2028-05-31 02:00–06:00 PDT
- Phasing: by POD / ASG (PD-1 -> PD-2 -> PD-3) with 30-min soak per phase
- Network gating: BGP route withdraw + short DNS TTL cutover to steer traffic to fallbacks during each phase
- Version pin: control plane pins via "shelve-token" config; automatic pin release after confirmed health checks or manual release
- Rollback: immediate traffic re-steer, shelve older image, and optional datastore read-only hold for 15m if KV inconsistency suspected

Attached is an initial playbook and a simple network-gate checklist. Please confirm whether the window works and whether DC-OPS needs any prep on your side.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-private-patch-playbook-v1.3.pdf, network-gate-checklist.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet maintenance: proposed dates and gating model

Stephanie — good summary. A few technical clarifications and additions from our side: 

1) Health tiers: we should require both service-level (500/latency) and model-quality signals (sampled inference correctness) before progressing the phase. I recommend a 5-min aggregated check window plus one synthetic transaction per region.

2) Pinning mechanism: we'll use a config map key "pin_version: v1.12.3" that, when set, forces the control plane to keep instances on the pinned runtime. The operator step will be: set pin -> withdraw BGP -> deploy -> validate -> release pin. We'll document the CLI commands in the runbook.

3) KV cache: plan to warm cache on new instances and avoid full invalidation; implement prefix-based invalidation for known keys touched by deployment. If we see cache miss storm, we will temporarily throttle the write path.

4) Fast rollback path: if metrics cross thresholds or model-output drift detected, we do: a) fail traffic back via BGP/DNS, b) set pin to previous image, c) abort canary and block auto-upgrade. If rollback doesn't recover within 20 minutes escalate to on-call infra.

I'll attach a short CLI snippet and suggested thresholds.

—Rishi
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

- Rehearsal: Fri 2028-05-26 09:00–11:00 PDT (staging cluster) — goal: full dry-run of pin/release and BGP withdraw with DataCenterCo in the loop.
- Phasing detail: we'll do PD-1 (us-west-2) -> PD-2 (us-west-1) -> PD-3 (on-prem DC). Each phase will include: 10m pre-checks, deploy (10m), 30m soak, post-checks (10m).
- BGP plan: DataCenterCo will perform the route withdraw; we'll coordinate a DNS TTL drop to 30s ten minutes before withdraw.

I'll create an orchestration checklist ticket and include step-by-step CLI commands.

Quick follow-up from infra automation: 

- We'll add a "shelve" flag to the deployment API so operators can pin older images without a full rollback. Implementation: PATCH /deploys/{cluster}/pin?shelf=true&image=v1.12.3 — this toggles the reconciler to keep existing nodes.
- Telemetry: add a synthetic that runs a verified prompt and checks token-level similarity; if similarity drops below 0.92 for two consecutive 5-min windows, trigger rollback. We'll wire this into the canary gates.
- Automation timeout: if a phase is paused manually for >60 minutes, automation will remove the BGP withdraw hold and revert DNS TTL to 300s to reduce operational risk.

I'll attach the staging-rehearsal-runbook.md with the sh scripts for pin/release and the CLI snippet.

—Vivek
Head of Private Deployments (Infra), Redwood Inference
